doc.title: Epic 16: Home Assistant Integration
doc.snippet: Add all required environment variables and configuration. Files: env.example, mcp_server/config.py, backend/api/config.py, docker-compose.yml. New Environment Variables include HA_URL, HA_ACCESS_TOKEN, HA_CONTROL_ALLOWLIST, HA_TIMEOUT, and MQTT configuration.

doc.title: Epic 16 Technical Specification
doc.snippet: Environment Variables for Epic 16: HA_URL, HA_ACCESS_TOKEN, HA_CONTROL_ALLOWLIST, HA_TIMEOUT for REST API; HA_MQTT_BROKER, HA_MQTT_PORT, HA_MQTT_USERNAME, HA_MQTT_PASSWORD, HA_MQTT_TOPICS, HA_MQTT_ALERT_USER_ID for MQTT.

doc.title: Project Documentation
doc.snippet: Setup instructions for environment variables. Required variables must be set in .env file. Sensitive variables are masked in logs. Docker Compose environment section defines variable passthrough from host.

doc.title: Environment Template
doc.snippet: Template file showing existing patterns for documenting environment variables with section headers, descriptions, defaults, and links to obtain API keys. SENSITIVE_VARS are masked in logging.

doc.title: Epic 16 Tech Spec
doc.snippet: Token Protection: HA_ACCESS_TOKEN and HA_MQTT_PASSWORD added to SENSITIVE_VARS (masked in logs). Principle of Least Privilege: Empty allowlist = no control operations permitted.

constraints.constraint: Follow existing patterns in config.py files using os.getenv() with sensible defaults

MCP server handles HA_URL, HA_ACCESS_TOKEN, HA_CONTROL_ALLOWLIST, HA_TIMEOUT
Backend handles HA_MQTT_* variables for MQTT subscriber service
Implement is_ha_configured() helper function to check if HA is properly configured
Unit tests should verify config loading and masking works correctly

tests.standards: Use pytest with pytest-asyncio for async tests. Follow existing test patterns in mcp_server/tests/ and backend/tests/unit/.
